subject: Transportation Systems
title: Cost vs. Conventional Rail
description: A quick win: understand Cost vs. Conventional Rail.

hook.text: Hyperloop promoters claim it will cost less than high-speed rail. Engineers are deeply skeptical.

buildup.text: Building a vacuum tube on pylons costs far more per mile than laying conventional high-speed track.

discovery.text: High-speed rail carries 1,000 passengers per train. Hyperloop pods carry 28 to 40. Throughput is harsh.

twist.text: To match one train's capacity, a hyperloop would need to launch pods every 30 seconds. That's unproven.

climax.text: Critics argue that hyperloop funding would be better spent on proven high-speed rail that works today.

punchline.text: The flashiest idea isn't always the smartest investment.

quiz.question: Why is hyperloop capacity a concern compared to high-speed rail?
options: Pods carry 28–40 passengers vs. 1,000 on a train, requiring very frequent launches
